directories.description: This instance's own reader-facing pages: the guide to writing a paper, which documents this instance's own process (`processes/content/authoring-a-paper.bpmn`). Composed THROUGH just-the-docs (`composed: true`, as the content core's own docs directory is), so its pages land in the platform's site under this instance's name with the sidebar, search and layout. `docs.json` here declares the `docs-source` the platform's one docs-page run reads: each `source/<group>-<slug>/` renders into `<group>/<slug>.md` beside it, and `compose-docs` leaves `source/` itself out.

The QA checkers this instance's Lean tooling provides, one folio-qa-checker/v1 node per criterion, naming COST_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS in pipeline/qa-checkers-cost.ts, and the maths checkers: VACUITY_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (Lean vacuity, four criteria), RENDER_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (render-math-mode-envelope), TRIVIALITY_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (proof-not-machine-trivial), EXTENDED_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (the paper proof-*, canonical-* and compute-* criteria), USES_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (uses-formal-coverage, lean-ref-owns-decl), Q_USAGE_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS in pipeline/qa-checkers-q-usage.ts (the seven q-usage-* criteria, run on their own by pipeline/q-usage-audit.ts) and WALL_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS in pipeline/qa-checkers-wall.ts (framework-canonical and the §7c archimedean wall: wall-side-correct, wall-base-ring-minimal). Registered for a folio by loadContributions through its dependency tree.

The ✍ suggest editor's checks and Crepe settings for this instance's content profiles, one folio-editor-checker/v1 node per profile naming the code (`path.ts#Export`) the editor loads. Today it holds one node: `paper-latex`, the LaTeX syntax checker and the Crepe repairs for paper math. The kind is declared in typologies/editor-checkers.json and its validator in validators/editor-checker.json.

The validators this instance's code provides, one folio-validator/v1 node each, naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks and the Zod export that checks it: `conjecture-register` for `folio-conjecture-register/v1` and `editor-checker` for `folio-editor-checker/v1`.

The generic pipeline slots this instance fills, one folio-pipeline-plugin/v1 node per slot, naming PIPELINE_IMPLEMENTATIONS in pipeline/plugin-slots.ts. Registered for a folio by loadContributions through its dependency tree.

The gettext side of folio-assistant-sci's own strings, one directory per target locale. `block-kinds.pot`/`.po`, the headings of the block kinds this instance declares in block-kinds/, keyed `msgctxt "block-kind:<kind>"` with the node's English `heading` as msgid, and `processes/<process>.pot`, the text of this layer's BPMN processes. Locale headings live in the translation graph, and kinds are not centrally managed, so the catalogue sits with the kinds rather than in cat-harness/translations/.

The paper adapter's math block kinds — the ones whose assertion is a formal mathematical claim (definition, theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, conjecture, proof), one folio-block-kind/v1 node per file. Kinds are discoverable and not centrally managed: cat-harness/schemas/block-kinds.ts finds these by scanning every instance's declared block-kinds graph.

The `mathpaper` block VOCABULARY's node, folio-content-adapter/v1: its name, its companion roles (md, ts, lean) and that cat-harness's code types it. The seven formal-claim kinds in block-kinds/ name it; core's document kinds name core's own `document` adapter. cat-harness/schemas/block-kinds.ts derives CONTENT_ADAPTERS from the typed nodes, and block-qa.ts derives ADAPTER_COMPANION_ROLES. The vocabulary is a node; the server adapter class stays in contentAdapters.
The graph typologies folio-assistant-sci owns, one folio-graph-typology/v1 node per file. There is no central registry for subgraph types: a harness declares its own in a kinds/ graph.

Ingested L1 source material for the sciences: `milnorlink`, the source text the `milnor-exposition-standard` skill reads; the Lean-autoformalization papers this layer's methodology nodes cite as `evidence`; papers on extracting mathematics from PDFs; and the CODATA 2022 constants table. `image-verdicts.json` holds the image-role judgements for this library's documents. The id is `library`, the conventional one, so this entry overrides the default rather than joining it: overrides match on id, never on path, so a distinct id at the same path would yield two entries for one directory and every fan-out consumer would scan it twice.

The reference lists of the papers in `library/`, split into one folio-reference/v1 node per entry with `provenance: extracted`. Each node is `<doc-id>.r<n>.json`, `<n>` being the printed number of a numbered list (so `[12]` in a paper's text is `.r12`) or the position in an author-year one; `derivedFrom` names the section file the entry was read from. GENERATED by scripts/extract-references.ts from the library text, never hand-edited: `check:extracted-references` fails on any difference. The text is PDF extraction, so the raw entry is always kept whole in `note`, and `title`, `author`, `issued`, `DOI` and `URL` are set only where the entry's shape makes them unambiguous; a field the extractor could not read with confidence is absent, not guessed. Listed and exported, with every other `references` directory, by folio-assistant-core's bibliography viewer.

The methodologies this layer adopts from its own library: external, named methods for formalising mathematics in Lean. A method belongs to the layer whose job it describes (`methodology-adoption` §4), so these sit apart from cat-harness's and core's methodologies. Each node renders the METHOD and states where the rendering stops; the paper's tools and numbers are not adopted.

directories.readOnlyBasis: NOT frozen, for the reason cat-harness gives for its own `skills` entry: most of this graph is authored here and edited, and the packages in it that are MATERIALIZED from a remote at a pinned commit each carry their own `materialization.json` with a sha256 per file, so `check:materialized-fixity` already fails an edit in place, file by file. Freezing the whole directory because some packages in it are materialized would freeze the skills this layer writes.
directories.description: The skills this layer owns: the paper content adapter's skills (`content/folio-paper-adapter/`, with `authoring-math`, `hypothesis-generation`, `scientific-critical-thinking` and `scientific-visualization` beside it), plus `lean/`, `data/` and the `voices/` subgraph, which `skills/skills.json` declares from within. Declared here explicitly on 2026-10-04 (bean `g2sv`, issue #2106). The directory was already reachable through the `skills` entry of `DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES`, which `ownDirectories` seeds for every instance and marks `declaredBy: (default)`, so `skill_list` already served its packages. A read-only analysis of the qou folio nonetheless reported it as undeclared and reachable only through `known-skills.ts`, because the declaration file was the only place the analysis looked, and that file said nothing. A convention is not visible from the declaration a reader opens, and a reader should not have to know the fallback to learn that this instance's largest graph exists. The id is `skills`, the CONVENTIONAL one, so this entry OVERRIDES the default rather than joining it. The reason is the one the `library` entry above gives: overrides match on id and never on path, so a distinct id at the same path would make two entries for one directory.

The PAPER content adapter: `PaperContentAdapter` and its Lean tool registrar, with its LaTeX, Lean and suggest code and its in-process tools. `dependents: skip` because a dependent gets its adapter by DECLARING a `contentType`, resolved through `BUILTIN_ADAPTERS` by variable path, rather than by inheriting this directory to scan.

This instance's scripts: its checkout checks (`check-lean-dirs.ts`, `check-editor-checkers.ts`, `check-workflows-security.ts`, `extract-references.ts`), Lean helpers (`setup-lean-toolchain.sh`, `lean-audit.ts`, `lean-coverage.ts`, `lsi-lean-decls.ts`), the Lean cache service (`lake-cache.sh` — the `lean-cache` tool — `reseed-lean-cache.sh`, `lake-cache-fetch.sh`, `lake-cache-produce.py`, `lake-cache-fetch-multi.py` and their `.bat` entry points, which only a Lean folio runs; they read and write the branch family `cat/folio-assistant-sci/lake-cache/<pkg>`), and `tests/`, which hold the harness's code, imported down from cat-harness, against this instance's paper processes, decision tables, pipeline plugins and contributed checkers.
directories._comment: A test pinning a paper diagram, `lean-lexer` or a contributed checker belongs to the instance that owns it. Same shape as folio-assistant-core's `scripts/`.

exempt.visualiser: No viewer by design. Each node is an outside package whose registry tarball and SPDX licence the node already links, so a viewer would only repeat the registry.

directories.title: Software libraries
directories.description: The outside libraries this layer's code imports: one `software-library/1.0.0` node per dependency in `package.json`, with the version and sha512 that `bun.lock` pins, the registry tarball, the SPDX licence read from the installed package, the range, whether it is a dev dependency, the files that import it (`usedBy`) and the `types/*.d.ts` shim that types it. GENERATED, never hand-edited: `bun run cat libraries:derive` writes it and `libraries:check` fails on a stale node, an import no node names, and a shim no node names. The kind is cat-harness's (one outside-software core shared with `tool-release`), and the writer and the gate are cat-harness-tools' (`scripts/libraries.ts`); this layer keeps its own nodes because it pins its own versions.

The Lean templates this harness's tooling fills: today `formal-edges.lean.tmpl`, which pipeline/formal-edges.ts writes into a folio's own `.lake/` and elaborates there. Declared with graph typology `lean`, the kind this instance owns for Lean sources (typologies/lean.json). The Tools (`lean-html-docs`, `lean-render-publish`), the process (`lean-docs-publish`) and the skill (`lean-html-docs`) are what a FOLIO's `lean` directory gets: its doc-gen4 render, published under the folio's site in the harness rail. `.tmpl`, never `.lean`: the platform tracks no Lean content, and lean-decl-starts-are-shared.test.ts holds it to that.

exempt.visualiser: This directory holds a Lean TEMPLATE, not a Lake package: there is nothing for doc-gen4 to elaborate, so there is no render to show. The visualiser the kind provides — the doc-gen4 render wrapped in the harness rail — belongs to a folio's `lean` directory, where a package is built; README.md here documents how a folio declares it.

directories.description: The PAPER profile of the files `folio_init` writes into a new folio: `paper/` holds the Lean build, lake-cache restore and blueprint workflows and the `.github/scripts` they call, written into a paper folio after the `document/` profile the tools layer keeps. Only a paper folio is given them, and the paper profile is this layer's. The id is the tools layer's `folio-templates`, so this directory is a member of that subgraph and `init-folio` finds it by id across the checkout, never by a path naming this layer. `{{assistant}}`, `{{folio}}`, `{{platform_git}}` and `{{platform_repo}}` are substituted at write time. Declared `code`: executable sources whose target is another repository. `dependents: skip` -- a folio inherits them through `folio_init`, not by owning a copy.

The science layer's Tool nodes. One `<id>/<id>.ts` (or `.json`) per folder: LaTeX build and checks, the Lean build, cache, audit and publish tools, and the proof-object tools. Reached by the harness through tool auto-discovery (cat-harness/tools/discover.ts), never by an import.

Source descriptors (`folio-source-descriptor/v1`): how to ENUMERATE Lean mathlib and ask it for a SUBSET. A descriptor is ABOUT one corpus and the instance that holds or catalogues that corpus owns it — the schema stays in cat-harness. Its far-apart sibling, WHO IRIS, is in who-iris: a mathlib declaration needs its import closure (`subsetIsSelfContained: false`), one identifier system, a local module graph.

The BPMN and DMN this layer OWNS: the paper's content processes, grouped by concern exactly as the harness groups its own (`processes/<group>/`, a DMN in `processes/<group>/decisions/`). `content/authoring-a-paper.bpmn` with `content/decisions/lean-build-gate.dmn`, `content/atomic-mass-drift-check.bpmn` and `content/lean-docs-publish.bpmn`. They name Lean and paper skills that live here, which cat-harness cannot reach. Their calls and skill refs that stay generic point DOWN through core to the harness.

Scenarios: the roles an actor takes on, in `roles.json`, the user stories told as them, in `stories.json`, and the actors in `actors/`. The compute-authoring-agent, lean-authoring-agent and proof-review-agent roles live here, and this layer's `address-*` voices point at them.

What auditing THIS instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean" — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. dependents: reproduce, because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another.

The judgement half of this instance's QA verdicts, kept on main: the `pair_attestations` that were carried inside its `kg-qa/v1` sidecars, one `qa-attestations/v1` file per subject at `kg-qa/<mirrored subject path>.attestations.json`. Schema: cat-harness `schemas/qa-attestations.ts`. dependents: reproduce, for the reason the `qa` entry gives.

Science's generated glossary (`glossary/generated/folio-assistant-sci/`): candidate `folio-glossary/v1` schemes extracted from this layer's tools, skills, BPMN activities and DMN decisions by core's `glossary:page`. A scheme is keyed by (instance, scheme), and each layer holds its own glossary.

Those tables are read at the CHECKOUT's pins, not at pins this instance's commit names, so no commit of it can hold the file current: it is built at publish and never committed.
